title: Timescale Separation Through the Lens of Operator Theory
summary: Timescale separation is a powerful tool for analyzing interconnected dynamical systems. Meanwhile, operator theory provides a general framework for studying the convergence of iterative methods formulated as fixed-point iterations, including algorithms arising in optimization, learning, and control. In this paper, we bridge these two areas by establishing timescale separation results for fixed-point iterations induced by both deterministic and stochastic operators.
